title: Chemical release
tldr: Move away from a chemical release and follow official instructions about evacuation or sheltering indoors. If exposed, get the chemical off and seek help. For severe symptoms, call emergency services; in the U.S., Poison Control is 1-800-222-1222.
steps: Do not approach a spill or plume to identify it.
The right action depends on the substance and where the release is; use location-specific instructions.
Follow Poison Control or responder instructions for removing contaminated clothing and washing; avoid spreading contamination to others.
Tell responders what was involved if known, your location and symptoms.
next: Wait for official clearance before returning. Keep contaminated items isolated as responders direct.
watch: A dust mask or N95 does not protect against toxic gases.
review_status: source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
without_help: If no reliable instruction arrives, move away from the visible release or affected area without passing through it. If leaving would put you into contaminated outdoor air, use an intact indoor space, shut openings and turn off outdoor-air intake while seeking trustworthy information. Do not identify a gas by sniffing it.
household: Keep the family together in the correct shelter for the hazard and separate potentially contaminated items from the living area. Use covered food and safe water. Prepare a bag for relocation, but do not send someone outside for it during an active release.
pack_now: Keep essential medicines, drinking water, a battery light, shoes, phone power and a written contact card within reach. Adapt the load to the hazard and the people with you; do not delay escape to collect equipment.
